context: Reviewed the original one-to-one iMessage exchanges. September 4: Instinct initiated check-in, confirmed completion and delivered a Wallet pass. When a different seat was requested, it reported that seat occupied, listed available alternatives and preserved the existing seat without charging. September 9: it alerted to a further fare drop, explained the difference against the post-credit fare and prepared repricing instructions without claiming the pending third-party call had completed. September 13: it confirmed check-in, kept the free assigned seat because only paid alternatives remained, and reported delivery of the airline boarding-pass link. Scores cover these observed outcomes; airline systems and reported earlier credits were not independently inspected. Private messages and travel/account identifiers are withheld.
